column1: Mark Rowe investigates attempts to reintroduce elms to Britain
column2: 马克·罗调查了人们为让榆树重返英国所作的尝试。

column1: Around 25 million elms, accounting for 90% of all elm trees in the UK, died during the 1960s and ’70s of Dutch elm disease.
column2: 20世纪60至70年代，英国约有2500万棵榆树死于荷兰榆树病，占当时全国榆树总数的90%。
column6: Dutch elm disease|n. 荷兰榆树病（榆枯萎病）

column1: In the aftermath, the elm, once so dominant in the British landscape, was largely forgotten.
column2: 此后，曾是英国风景中占据主导地位的榆树，在很大程度上被人们淡忘了。
column3: In the aftermath|在这场灾害过后

column1: However, there’s now hope the elm may be reintroduced to the countryside of central and southern England.
column2: 不过，如今人们有望把榆树重新引入英格兰中部和南部的乡村。

column1: Any reintroduction will start from a very low base.
column2: 重新引种只能从很低的起点开始。

column1: ‘The impact of the disease is difficult to picture if you hadn’t seen what was there before,’ says Matt Elliot of the Woodland Trust.
column2: 英国林地信托基金会的马特·埃利奥特说：“如果没见过这里从前的样子，就很难想象这场树病造成了多大影响。”
column6: Woodland Trust|英国林地信托基金会

column1: ‘You look at old photographs from the 1960s and it’s only then that you realise the impact [elms had] ... They were significant, large trees ... then they were gone.’
column2: “看看20世纪60年代的老照片，你这才会明白榆树当年有多重要……那些树高大醒目……后来就这么消失了。”
column7: significant|adj. 重要的，引人注目的

column1: The disease is caused by a fungus that blocks the elms’ vascular (water, nutrient and food transport) system, causing branches to wilt and die.
column2: 这种病由一种真菌引起。真菌会堵塞榆树的维管系统，也就是输送水分、养分和食物的系统，导致树枝萎蔫、枯死。

column1: A first epidemic, which occurred in the 1920s, gradually died down, but in the ’70s a second epidemic was triggered by shipments of elm from Canada.
column2: 20世纪20年代，树病首次大规模流行，后来渐渐平息。但到了70年代，从加拿大运来的榆木又引发了第二次大流行。
column3: epidemic|n. 疾病的大规模流行

column1: The wood came in the form of logs destined for boat building and its intact bark was perfect for the elm bark beetles that spread the deadly fungus.
column2: 运来的是准备用于造船的原木，树皮完好无损，恰好适合传播这种致命真菌的榆小蠹虫栖身。
column3: in the form of|以……的形式
column7: elm bark beetles|n. 榆小蠹虫

column1: This time, the beetles carried a much more virulent strain that destroyed the vast majority of British elms.
column2: 这一次，小蠹虫携带的菌株致病力强得多，英国绝大多数榆树都因此枯死。
column8: the vast majority of|绝大多数

column1: Today, elms still exist in the southern English countryside but mostly only in low hedgerows between fields.
column2: 如今，英格兰南部乡间仍能看到榆树，但大多只长在田块之间低矮的树篱里。

column1: ‘We have millions of small elms in hedgerows but they get targeted by the beetle as soon as they reach a certain size,’ says Karen Russell, co-author of the report ‘Where we are with elm’.
column2: 《榆树现状》报告的合著者凯伦·拉塞尔说：“树篱里有数百万棵小榆树，可它们一长到一定大小，就会被小蠹虫盯上。”
column5: get targeted by|成为……攻击的目标

column1: Once the trunk of the elm reaches 10–15 centimetres or so in diameter, it becomes a perfect size for beetles to lay eggs and for the fungus to take hold.
column2: 榆树树干的直径一到十至十五厘米左右，粗细就恰好适合小蠹虫产卵，也适合真菌在树体内生长。
column9: take hold|开始牢固立足，扩展

column1: Yet mature specimens have been identified, in counties such as Cambridgeshire, that are hundreds of years old, and have mysteriously escaped the epidemic.
column2: 然而，人们在剑桥郡等地发现了一些树龄已有数百年的成熟榆树，它们躲过了这场病害，原因不明。
column9: epidemic|n. 疾病的大规模流行

column1: The key, Russell says, is to identify and study those trees that have survived and work out why they stood tall when millions of others succumbed.
column2: 拉塞尔说，关键在于找出并研究那些幸存的榆树，弄清为什么其他数百万棵树纷纷病死，它们却依然挺立。

column1: Nevertheless, opportunities are limited as the number of these mature survivors is relatively small.
column2: 不过，这样的研究机会有限，因为存活至今的成熟榆树数量相对较少。

column1: ‘What are the reasons for their survival?’ asks Russell.
column2: “它们为什么能活下来？”拉塞尔问道。

column1: ‘Avoidance, tolerance, resistance?
column2: “是避开了感染，是能耐受病害，还是有抗病能力？

column1: We don’t know where the balance lies between the three.
column2: 我们还不知道这三个因素各起了多大作用。
column3: balance|n. 各因素的相对比重

column1: I don’t see how it can be entirely down to luck.’
column2: 我不相信这完全靠运气。”

column1: For centuries, elm ran a close second to oak as the hardwood tree of choice in Britain and was in many instances the most prominent tree in the landscape.
column2: 几个世纪以来，论英国人选用硬木树种的偏好，榆树紧随橡树之后。在许多地方，它还是风景中最醒目的树。
column4: ran a close second to|仅次于……，与之相差无几
column8: in many instances|在许多情况下

column1: Not only was elm common in European forests, it became a key component of birch, ash and hazel woodlands.
column2: 榆树不仅在欧洲森林中很常见，也是桦树、白蜡树和榛树林地中的重要树种。
column3: Not only|不但（句首引起倒装）
column5: key component|n. 重要组成部分

column1: The use of elm is thought to go back to the Bronze Age, when it was widely used for tools.
column2: 人们认为，榆木的使用可以追溯到青铜时代，当时它被广泛用来制作工具。

column1: Elm was also the preferred material for shields and early swords.
column2: 榆木也是制作盾牌和早期刀剑的首选材料。

column1: In the 18th century, it was planted more widely and its wood was used for items such as storage crates and flooring.
column2: 18世纪，榆树种植得更加广泛，榆木被用来制作储物板条箱、地板等物品。

column1: It was also suitable for items that experienced high levels of impact and was used to build the keel of the 19th-century sailing ship Cutty Sark as well as mining equipment.
column2: 榆木也适合制作需要承受强烈冲击的物件。19世纪帆船“卡蒂萨克”号的龙骨以及采矿设备就用榆木制成。
column4: high levels of impact|很强的冲击力

column1: Given how ingrained elm is in British culture, it’s unsurprising the tree has many advocates.
column2: 榆树在英国文化中深深扎了根，这种树拥有众多支持者，也就不足为奇了。

column1: Amongst them is Peter Bourne of the National Elm Collection in Brighton.
column2: 其中一位便是彼得·伯恩，他来自布赖顿的英国国家榆树收藏机构。
column4: collection|n. 收藏（此指活树收藏）

column1: ‘I saw Dutch elm disease unfold as a small boy,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“我小时候亲眼见过荷兰榆树病是怎样一步步蔓延的。”
column3: Dutch elm disease|n. 荷兰榆树病

column1: ‘The elm seemed to be part of rural England, but I remember watching trees just lose their leaves and that really stayed with me.’
column2: “榆树仿佛就是英格兰乡村的一部分。我还记得眼看着那些树的叶子掉光，那一幕一直印在我脑海里。”
column7: stayed with me|留在某人的记忆中

column1: Today, the city of Brighton’s elms total about 17,000.
column2: 如今，布赖顿市约有一万七千棵榆树。

column1: Local factors appear to have contributed to their survival.
column2: 当地的一些条件似乎帮助这些榆树存活了下来。

column1: Strong winds from the sea make it difficult for the determined elm bark beetle to attack this coastal city’s elm population.
column2: 海上吹来的强风使顽强的榆小蠹虫很难侵袭这座海滨城市的榆树群。
column4: elm bark beetle|n. 榆小蠹虫

column1: However, the situation is precarious.
column2: 不过，眼下的形势并不稳定。
column5: precarious|adj. 不稳定的，岌岌可危的

column1: ‘The beetles can just march in if we’re not careful, as the threat is right on our doorstep,’ says Bourne.
column2: 伯恩说：“我们稍不留神，这些甲虫就会长驱直入，因为威胁就在家门口。”
column7: on our doorstep|就在某人的家门口，近在眼前

column1: Any prospect of the elm returning relies heavily on trees being either resistant to, or tolerant of, the disease.
column2: 榆树能否回归，在很大程度上取决于榆树是否具有抗病性或耐病性。
column4: relies heavily on|在很大程度上取决于
column5: either|conj. 或者（与 or 呼应）

column1: This means a widespread reintroduction would involve existing or new hybrid strains derived from resistant, generally non-native elm species.
column2: 这意味着，要大范围重新引种，就得采用现有或新育成的杂交品系。这些品系源自有抗病性的榆树种，而这些树种大多并非本土物种。

column1: A new generation of seedlings have been bred and tested to see if they can withstand the fungus by cutting a small slit on the bark and injecting a tiny amount of the pathogen.
column2: 研究者已培育出新一代幼苗，并对其进行测试，看它们能否抵御这种真菌。测试时，他们在树皮上划开一个小口，注入微量病原体。

column1: ‘The effects are very quick,’ says Russell.
column2: 拉塞尔说：“很快就能看出结果。”

column1: ‘You return in four to six weeks and trees that are resistant show no symptoms, whereas those that are susceptible show leaf loss and may even have died completely.’
column2: “四到六周后再来看，抗病的树没有症状，而易感的树已经落叶，有的甚至可能整株都枯死了。”
column3: in four to six weeks|四至六周后

column1: All of this raises questions of social acceptance, acknowledges Russell.
column2: 拉塞尔承认，这一切都牵涉到公众能否接受的问题。

column1: ‘If we’re putting elm back into the landscape, a small element of it is not native – are we bothered about that?’
column2: “如果我们把榆树重新引入这片土地，它会带有少量非本土成分。我们介意这一点吗？”

column1: For her, the environmental case for reintroducing elm is strong.
column2: 在她看来，从环境角度讲，重新引种榆树的理由很充分。
column6: strong|adj. 理由充分、有说服力的

column1: ‘They will host wildlife, which is a good thing.’
column2: “这些树会为野生生物提供栖息地，这是好事。”

column1: Others are more wary.
column2: 另一些人则更加谨慎。
column4: wary|adj. 谨慎的，心存戒备的

column1: ‘On the face of it, it seems like a good idea,’ says Elliot.
column2: 埃利奥特说：“乍看之下，这似乎是个好主意。”
column3: On the face of it|从表面上看，乍看之下

column1: The problem, he suggests, is that, ‘You’re replacing a native species with a horticultural analogue*.
column2: 他指出，问题在于：“你用一种园艺培育的近似种替代了本土物种。
column6: horticultural analogue|n. 与原物种遗传相近的栽培植物

column1: You’re effectively cloning.’
column2: 实际上，你是在克隆。”

column1: There’s also the risk of introducing new diseases.
column2: 此外，还存在引入新病害的风险。

column1: Rather than plant new elms, the Woodland Trust emphasises providing space to those elms that have survived independently.
column2: 英国林地信托基金会主张给那些自行存活下来的榆树留出生长空间，而非另栽新树。
column5: Woodland Trust|英国林地信托基金会
column9: independently|adv. 独立地，靠自身力量

column1: ‘Sometimes the best thing you can do is just give nature time to recover ... over time, you might get resistance,’ says Elliot.
column2: 埃利奥特说：“有时，最好的做法就是给自然一些时间去恢复……时间久了，也许就会出现抗病性。”
column3: give nature time to|给大自然时间去……
